title: A frame's columns start where its padding does
goal: Give a frame 12 points of padding, switch its columns on, and the columns do not start at 12: they start wherever the Columns section's own Margin says, which is 32 out of the box. So the red columns do not sit inside the padding, and rectangles the frame places at 12 do not line up with them. One frame has one inset from its edge, and the columns should be drawn inside it rather than measured from a second number that nobody connected to the first.
notes:
Reported by the user on 2026-09-09: "i have padding of 12 on all sides in a frame. i say show columns, but the columns do not have 12 padding on all sides. additionally i put some rects in it, they do not align with the red column shown. i think the column is off."

Cause, confirmed by reading (not yet reproduced in the app - reproduce first and record the numbers). The column arithmetic is not wrong; it is measuring from a DIFFERENT number than the frame's padding. Two independent values describe the same edge:
1. GroupLayout.padding (Sources/PhotonzCore/GroupLayout.swift:101), a GroupPadding with four sides (:413), which is what insets the frame's contents.
2. FrameColumns.margin (Sources/PhotonzCore/FrameColumns.swift:62), a single number defaulting to 32 (:44), which is what the columns are measured from: bands(inWidth:) at :106 computes content = width - margin * 2.
Nothing links them. So padding 12 with the default margin puts the columns at 32 and the laid-out rects at 12, which is exactly the misalignment reported.

Three separate consequences, all from the same root, and the fix must cover all three:
- The columns start at the wrong x.
- There is no vertical inset at ALL. bands(in screen:) at FrameColumns.swift:126 builds each band as y: screen.minY, height: screen.height, so the bands run the full height of the frame whatever the padding is. That is why the user says the columns do not have 12 on all sides: they cannot have any top or bottom inset today.
- Margin is ONE number applied to both sides equally, while GroupPadding has four. So even typing 12 into Margin cannot match padding that differs per side.

Recommended shape, but the runner owns the call and must justify it in the audit: make the columns derive their inset from the frame's padding and retire the separate Margin field, because two numbers for one edge is the bug rather than a symptom of it. The migration question is the real work: documents already carry a margin, and FrameColumns is Codable and saved with the document. Decide and record whether an existing margin is dropped, kept as a fallback for a frame with no padding, or written into the frame's padding on load; whichever is chosen, an existing document must not silently move its columns under somebody without that being a deliberate, stated migration.

The drawing and the snapping read the same arithmetic, so fixing it once fixes both: the chrome is CanvasColumnChrome.swift:51 calling columns.bands(in: box), and the drag pull is PhotonzDocument.columnBands(excluding:) at FrameColumns.swift:178 calling the same thing. Do not fix one of them.

Also check EditorState+Frames.swift:341, which reports the column width shown in the Columns section footnote via bands(inWidth:); it has to keep agreeing with what is drawn after the change, or the panel will print a width the canvas does not have.

Built by two tasks that are already done ('a-screen-can-show-the-column-grid-you-are-design' and 'the-columns-section-and-the-show-columns-menu-ro'), neither of which connected columns to padding.

Check Sources/Photonz/Releases/ before assuming one change reaches both releases; per CLAUDE.md a Current change is not finished until Next has it.
acceptance: Reproduce it first with numbers: a frame with padding 12 on all sides and columns switched on, and record where the first column's left edge actually falls and where it should
With padding of 12 on all sides, the first column starts 12 from the left edge and the last column ends 12 from the right edge, measured off a render rather than by eye
The columns are inset from the top and bottom by the padding too, so a frame padded on all sides does not have columns running edge to edge vertically
Padding that differs per side is honoured per side: 12 left and 24 right puts the first column at 12 and the last one ending 24 in
A rectangle the frame lays out at the padding edge lines up exactly with the first column's edge, checked by sampling the rendered pixels
Changing the padding moves the columns immediately, with no second number to update
A frame that has no padding behaves as it does today, so existing documents do not shift under people
Say in the audit what happened to the existing Margin number and to documents that carry one: whether it is gone, kept as a fallback, or migrated, and why
Tests in PhotonzCore for the band arithmetic against padding, including asymmetric padding and a padding that leaves no room, written before the change
Audit under queue/audits/ with a captured frame at padding 12 showing the columns and a laid-out rectangle agreeing, anything rough filed as a follow-up
